title: Horizon Europe Launches €5M ($5.67M USD) Q-VERSE Consortium to Build Hardware-Agnostic Quantum Software Stack - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Horizon Europe launched Q-VERSE, a 36-month, €5M, 13-partner consortium coordinated by Fraunhofer FOKUS to build an open, vendor-agnostic quantum software stack on Eclipse Qrisp with OpenQASM/QIR runtimes, AI-driven hybrid orchestration and five industrial pilots.

insights.claim: Q-VERSE aims to decouple high-level quantum application development from low-level QPU architectures across gate-based processors, annealers and HPC clusters via an open, vendor-agnostic stack.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware abstraction reduces vendor lock-in, pressuring proprietary SDK moats of hardware vendors.
insights.quote: decouple high-level quantum application development from low-level physical QPU architectures
insights.locator: The European Commission has launched Q-VERSE

insights.claim: The stack uses Eclipse Qrisp as its high-level language and combines OpenQASM and LLVM-based QIR intermediate representations to support runtime discovery of QPU gate sets, connectivity graphs and noise profiles.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Standard IRs could become the interoperability layer of the quantum software market.

insights.claim: The project is funded with €5 million ($5.67M) over 36 months under the European Quantum Flagship with 13 partners including Multiverse Computing, DB Systel, Eclipse Foundation, OTE and Tecnalia.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Modest EU funding; a signal of policy direction rather than a market mover.
insights.locator: The European Commission has launched Q-VERSE

themes.theme: AI for hybrid orchestration and testing

insights.claim: Q-VERSE plans AI-driven hybrid orchestration using graph neural networks and reinforcement learning to split workloads, plus transfer-learning noise models and automated probabilistic flaw detection.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI-quantum convergence in orchestration is an emerging software niche.

insights.claim: Validation will occur across five industrial pilots against real NISQ constraints, including DB Systel railway dispatch scheduling, financial portfolio optimization, pharmaceutical molecular design and telecom analytics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Industrial pilots indicate which sectors European quantum software targets first.
insights.locator: Simula Research Laboratory leads Work Package 4
